texts: I have read a hundred books on romance and still froze when she smiled at me. Write a doha about how deep affection comes only by feeling, never by study, tied together by one fine thread.
Affection is a silken thread spun in the heart, and no scholar's pen has ever learned to weave it.
thread of devotion
My cousin earned every degree there is but never learned to care for her husband the way the village cook cares for her goats, without any thread of instruction.
can you do a doha on how caring for someone is felt not studied, maybe with a thread in it
We stayed one night at a tiny inn on the highway, and the owner's quiet care for his sick wife taught me more than any novel.
Tenderness is the one guest the inn of the heart welcomes without a ledger or a fee.
devotion at the inn

After years of dusty reading, the old professor still could not say what his wife meant to him until she was gone. Compose a couplet showing affection is lived, not learned, with a roadside inn as the setting.
a short doha please, deep affection cant be taught, set it at some old inn
Two and a half syllables of the heart outweigh all the learning that wise men ever gathered.
My daughter keeps asking which course will teach her to adore someone, and I just laugh and tell her to wait and see.

Teach me a verse about how the whole library of the world cannot show a person how to truly cherish another, because that lesson is given only by the heart in living moments and never by pages of any kind.
doha about the one lesson no school can give, caring deeply for someone
unlearned tenderness

I want a doha for my brother's wedding about how deep devotion cannot be studied from scriptures or poems, and how two people crossing life together must learn it by rowing side by side in a small boat of trust.
hey, need a doha about love you cant learn from books, put a boat in it
devotion in one boat
He never read a single poem, yet every dawn he rows his old wife across to her clinic in a wooden boat and waits all day.
Two hearts in one boat need no map; the tide of tenderness teaches what no teacher can.
My father never said he cared, but at the funeral that huge silent elephant of a man carried her bier alone and no one dared to help.
bier, elephant, tenderness
doha plz: unspoken devotion at a funeral, a bier and an elephant of a man
On the bier lay a lifetime of unspoken tenderness, and the elephant of a man bowed like a child.

Compose a couplet about the day my mother passed: her bier was lifted, and my father, who never spoke fondly, stood like a wounded elephant, proving that real affection is never taught by words or by books.
how do you teach someone to adore another? you cant, doha on that
The learned reader stays poor beside the one who has simply tasted a heart's affection.
hey could u write a doha on how nobody can read their way into caring for someone, it just happens to you when it happens, whether or not you have studied a thousand pages of poems
unread tenderness
When my grandmother, who never went to school, held my crying cousin all night, I understood what none of my textbooks ever explained.
Our parrot recites the romantic songs from the radio every sunrise, but my old landlord just brings his bedridden wife tea and says nothing.
parrot and sun, tenderness
A parrot may recite the verses of passion all day and never feel the warmth the sun gives a sleeping heart.
doha: parrot repeating sweet words vs real feeling under the sun

The parrot in our courtyard repeats verses of romance he never understood, while my neighbor under the morning sun feels it silently for his wife. Write a doha about that gap between memorized words and real affection.
My uncle memorised every romance in the language but treated his wife like a snake in the grass, cold and sharp, never once learning.

A snake can sit coiled around a fragrant branch without knowing its scent, as a scholar can quote ten books without knowing how to cherish someone. Please write a doha capturing this unlearnable tenderness.
a doha pls, deep affection cannot be taught, add a snake somewhere
devotion and the snake
The snake coils round fragrance and never learns it; so the learned hold affection in books and miss it in the heart.
doha on affection that books cant teach, use a bitter gourd for it
The bitter gourd hears lectures on sweetness yet stays bitter, until true tenderness melts it from within.
bitter gourd, sweet heart

Please write a couplet about affection that no one can learn from reading, comparing it to how a bitter gourd stays bitter however many scholars explain sweetness to it, until the heart itself is changed.
My stern aunt, bitter as a gourd about everything, softened completely the day her first grandchild was placed in her arms.
oh write a doha on affection thats not learnt from books, bee and net would be nice

A bee hovers around flowers in a garden covered by a net, caught between desire and caution. Write a doha showing real affection is not learned from scholars but gets you stuck, sweetly, like that bee in a net.
The bee falls into the net of the flower and calls the trap sweetness; such is the lesson no teacher can give.
My friend was a careful planner until she fell for the neighbor's son, and now she buzzes around him like a bee tangled in a net.
bee, net, tenderness
the lesson not in books
short doha, caring for someone isnt something school teaches
My neighbor holds a doctorate in literature but could not tell his dying mother he cherished her until her last night.

Please write a doha explaining that even all the learning of ten great universities cannot make a person know how to truly care for another, because that knowing is awakened only by living through it with them.
One syllable of the heart's affection is worth more than all the wisdom that pundits have spoken.
a doha pls, peacock dancing and a market selling books of romance

A peacock dances for the rain with no manual, while the market sells guidebooks on romance but never sells tenderness. Write a doha about affection that cannot be bought in the market or learned from a book.
I wandered through the market looking for a book on how to adore my new husband, and a peacock feather seller laughed and said just look at him.
The peacock dances unrehearsed while the market sells guidebooks of romance; the heart owns what no stall can offer.
peacock, market, tenderness
a bell, a heart
bell + devotion lesson doha, no book can teach it
A quiet old man comes every dusk to ring the bell for his late wife, and he never had a single lesson in how to adore.
A bell rings the devotion no reading can teach; so does the heart when it meets its beloved.
Please compose a doha about how deep affection cannot be taught in any classroom, and how even a bell rings out its devotion without needing to read a single page.
The traveler on the rope does not read how to trust; his beloved's hand teaches him mid-fall.
doha plz, a traveler learns real affection not from books but from a rope pulled tight
My traveler friend crossed the old rope over the gorge after three months without a word, and my aunt just held his face and neither said anything.
rope, traveler, tenderness
Compose a doha about a traveler walking a rope stretched over a gorge who learns to cherish another not from teachers but from slipping and being caught by a hand, as real trust is always learned.
My grandmother stitched my wedding dress herself with a small needle, adding a pearl at each seam, and never read a book on affection. Write a doha about learning tenderness by doing, not studying.
The needle that stitches a pearl has learned no scripture, yet it binds two lives better than a scholar.
needle and pearl
My grandmother mended my torn school uniform every Sunday with a tiny needle and a loose pearl button, never once telling me she cared.
a doha about affection thats not learnt, with a needle and a pearl in it
The bridge of hearts is built by crossing it, and hardship alone is the touchstone of what was learned.
Please compose a doha about how the bridge between two hearts is built by living, not by study, and how only the touchstone of real hardship proves whether the affection between them is genuine.
hey a doha: care is proven in hard times, bridge and touchstone pls
They were tested when she lost her job and the savings ran out; that crossing, a rickety bridge with no touchstone but trust, showed more than ten years of reading poems together.
bridge and touchstone
The lock of the heart yields not to a thousand scholars, but opens to one gentle breath of tenderness.
Write me a doha in which affection is a lock that no scholar can pick with books or arguments, though one gentle touch from the right heart opens it effortlessly, without any teaching at all.
the lock of devotion
The professor could solve any riddle in his field but no one could open the lock on his silent heart until his student's kindness did it.
caring cant be learned doha with a lock motif plz

I have spent my life studying poetry and philosophy but never knew how to feel for another until a stranger sat beside me in sorrow and I forgot all I had read. Please write a doha for this unlearnable thing.
You may know the whole world and still stand a beginner where the heart alone is the teacher.
At my retirement party, the man who had read everything in the library told me his one regret is never learning how to be close to people.
heart as teacher
please write a doha, deep affection is unteachable, nothing in books

Write a doha in the voice of a parrot trained to say sweet words, who learns that real affection cannot be recited, and only begins to know it when a lonely old woman feeds him each morning with care.
The parrot knew the words by heart but not the heart; then a hand fed him kindly, and he understood.
do a doha, parrot mimics tender words but real feeling is different
Our tamed parrot says sweet things all day long, but it was the old widow's patient feeding that taught him what the phrases are for.
the parrot who learned
a doha about unlearned tenderness, a bier on stone, grief of a hard man
At my father's funeral they lowered the bier gently onto a stone slab and I saw how a hard man's hands trembled over a grief he never could name. Write a doha on tenderness that no one teaches.
bier on stone
My brother never hugged anyone, but when our mother's bier was lifted, he sat on the stone steps and cried like a boy.
The bier is set on cold stone, and the hands that never learned to say it tremble with all they felt.
Learning falls silent where the heart speaks, and the learned stand like children before it.
unlearned affection
I tried reading advice columns for months to understand my husband's silence, but the answer came the evening I just sat beside him.
dohe on why caring can't be studied
What is it that no master can teach the pupil, the one subject where every scholar remains a beginner and only the willing heart ever graduates, whatever the learning behind it?
I keep telling my students that all the textbooks in the world can describe affection but never deliver it, and I would be happy with a doha capturing that the heart has to be touched, not taught.
touch, not teaching
I taught literature for thirty years and wept like a fool the first time my granddaughter put her small fingers around my thumb.
doha on how a teacher cannot teach caring, only the heart can
Describe it however you wish, the heart will never know affection until the heart is touched.
The village potter and his wife can't read a word, but she hums while he works and he stops mid-task to listen.
Without scripture or scholar, one shared glance becomes an epic the pundits cannot match.
short chat style doha, uneducated couple who understand each other perfectly
unstudied devotion

Between two simple villagers there was never a scripture studied, yet the glances across the courtyard were a whole epic. Write for me a doha praising that unstudied devotion that grows on its own without books.
My mother heated milk at midnight whenever I had a fever, and she never once asked whether she was tired or whether it was her duty.
milk of tenderness
doha about a mothers unlearned care, milk for a sick child
The milk of kindness flows not from scripture but from a mother's breast, and no scholar has bottled it.

I once watched a mother heat milk for her sick child through the whole night, never having studied a single book on affection, only moved by what was in her. Compose a doha celebrating this unlearned devotion.
The charming man who learned every pickup trick from magazines lost her to a quiet boy who remembered her mother's name, no net or technique needed.
The net catches the swimmer, not the heart; the heart is caught by one look that no tutor ever showed.
affection cant be caught with tricks, doha w a net
net and the heart
Compose a doha showing how a net can trap a swimmer but never the heart, which is captured only by simple devotion and never by clever study, technique, or learned tricks from any guide.
Soft as cotton, rooted like a tree, two hearts learned in silence what the learned never found in print.
cotton and the tree
They met under an old tree beside a cotton field and have been married for fifty years without ever reading a manual on how.

Please write a doha about the cotton fields and the tall tree where two villagers met without ever reading what devotion should look like; just the soft way they leaned on each other taught them everything.
doha: unlearned devotion between two villagers, tree and cotton
Please give me a doha about a feeling so deep that all the volumes in every library only point towards it and never reach it, because the only school for it is the heart itself, taught by living.
doha: no library can teach you how to care
beyond learning
Ever since I stopped googling how to make my partner happy and simply listened to her day, things have become so much softer between us.
All the learning of the world only points the way; the heart alone can walk it.
The rainbird on the branch cries for a single drop, and nobody taught it that longing. Compose a doha about devotion not learned in schools but born in the throat of a bird that waits.
rainbird's lesson
I used to think my grandfather's daily letters to my grandmother were silly, then I saw how the rainbird in his garden cried the same way.
doha with a rainbird waiting for rain, about a feeling nobody teaches
The rainbird was never taught to wait for its one raindrop; the heart too knows by being, not by reading.

Write a doha that says the sharpest scholar sits mute before the simplest act of cherishing someone, because understanding that act requires giving up cleverness and simply being present with the person you adore.
cleverness laid down
Our teacher knew every theory about relationships, yet his own wife left him; the plumber next to us has been happily married for forty years.
doha on wisdom vs real caring, you learn it by being there
The cleverest minds fall silent before a single act of cherishing, which is learned by laying cleverness down.
My uncle thinks affection is something you read about in poems, but my aunt has been showing him daily, silently, with simple chai.
Last winter my aunt who never studied past fifth grade nursed her estranged husband through a long illness and forgave him with nothing but a bowl of soup. Write a doha on that lived tenderness.
a patient hand
No teaching was needed at his side; a patient hand did what a thousand verses could not.
plz doha: real care at a sickbed, nothing studied
Two weeks after the arranged wedding my cousin was ill, and her husband, who barely knew her, sat up all night with cold compresses.
My friend asked how to learn to adore a spouse in an arranged marriage, and I said it cannot be taught: you simply live together and the feeling arrives. Write a doha in that spirit, long and gentle.
doha: affection grows after marriage, you cant study it
Strangers at the altar, then companions for life; the heart is the only teacher that never tires.
arranged and awakening

The priest taught the child verses of devotion and the child recited every line, but only when the evening shadow lengthened over his grandmother's courtyard did he feel what the verses meant. Please write a doha.
The priest gives the verse; the long shadow of evening gives the meaning, and the heart quietly learns.
the priest's shadow
a doha: a priest learns real affection not from scripture, with a long shadow
Our priest has read all the scriptures on devotion, but it was his shadow, the old dog that follows him everywhere, that taught him what it means.
My mother made butter every morning with a churn so I would have something on my roti, and that was her whole way of saying it.
The woman churning curd every dawn never read a poem, yet the rhythm of her arm is a song of devotion. Write a doha where the churn teaches that tenderness comes through labor and quiet daily duty.
The churn turns and butter rises; so does devotion rise from the daily labor of caring that no scholar rehearsed.
the churn's song
doha about a woman at a churn, quiet daily care, no book needed
My cousin said it hit him like an arrow when he saw her walk along the river, and he knew without a book what had happened to him.
the arrow and the river
I was walking by the river when I saw an old man pierced by an arrow of grief sit beside his wife's memorial. He had never studied devotion, but his sorrow taught him. Write a doha for this.
can u write a doha, feeling hits like an arrow near a river, nobody teaches it
The river runs on unschooled, and the arrow of true feeling pierces without a master.
She never read a thing about devotion, but every year she polishes his old sword, and she lights up when the bus from the border arrives.
Compose a doha for a soldier's wife who learns the truth of devotion not from scripture but from the sword hanging unused on her husband's wall, because to cherish another is also to wait for them.
doha for a soldiers wife, with his sword
the soldier's sword
The sword hangs on the wall and the wife waits; the heart learns what no scholar will teach in books.

Write a poem in two lines about the way the heart learns to care. Not by lessons or lectures, but slowly, secretly, without any teacher at all, while the person is not even paying attention to what is happening.
doha on how caring creeps up on you, nobody teaches it
learning without lessons
Unseen, unplanned, the heart learns its way without a teacher, and only afterwards calls it by name.
At twenty I laughed at the idea of tenderness, but then I watched my sister gently care for her newborn and understood I knew nothing.
washerman, soft clouds
The washerman's hard hands know the riverbank, yet go soft as a cloud for the one they cherish.
The washerman beats clothes on the riverbank while a cloud drifts over him, yet when he looks at his wife his rough hands go soft. Write a doha about the unlearned tenderness in a hardworking man.
doha on a rough hardworking man tender at heart, washerman and clouds
The washerman near our lane is rough with everyone but sings under the cloud cover whenever his wife brings his lunch.
The goldsmith measures gold to a grain, yet one smile of the beloved outweighs the whole shop.
My uncle the jeweller can value any gold necklace in a second, but he has never been able to explain what it feels like when his daughter laughs.
gold and the smile
doha: affection cant be weighed like gold
The goldsmith can weigh gold to the grain but cannot weigh the worth of a smile. Please write a doha on how affection cannot be priced, taught, or measured by the cleverest of men in any trade.
No guru can hand it over and no scripture can promise it; the heart, once open, is its own master.
the heart's own teacher
Is there any scripture, teacher, or school that can show a person the way to cherish someone with their whole being? Please give me a doha that answers no, and says only the heart can teach itself.
After years of therapy and self-help my brother admitted that what finally taught him how to be kind was a stray puppy.
doha: can anyone teach you to adore someone? nope
a seed of affection
My daughter planted a seed in a cup and talked to it daily, and I realised she was learning something about care that I never taught her.
doha about how affection sprouts on its own like a seed
A seed buried in the ground does not read a manual on how to grow toward the light. Please write a doha that sees the beginning of affection in the heart as a seed that sprouts all by itself.
The seed does not study the sky yet reaches for it; the heart too grows toward its beloved unschooled.
Pages upon pages explain it; an hour beside the beloved lives it, and the lived hour outweighs them all.
Could you offer a doha on this thought: ten thousand pages of philosophy may explain affection, but a single hour sitting beside someone you cherish teaches what the pages cannot reach?
doha for quiet togetherness that no book describes
an hour beside you
Last Diwali my husband and I sat quietly on the terrace with no phones, and I learned more about us in that hour than in a year of talk.
My neighbor sells pearls in the market all day yet sleeps on the hospital floor beside his wife and refuses to leave even for tea.
In the old market a pearl merchant told me he had sold jewels for forty years, but the day his wife fell ill he learned the dearest pearl was her hand in his. Please write a doha about it.
doha with a pearl seller and a market, learning real devotion the hard way
Pearls are traded in the market by weight, but a hand held in sickness is a jewel no merchant can sell.
pearl and the market
short doha pls, this feeling is not something books can tell you
I remember first meeting my husband; I stopped reciting what I rehearsed and just stared, all my reading gone out of my head.
Not in print and not in teaching, it arrives uninvited and is known on sight.
unlearned devotion
yo can u make a doha on affection that is not found in books, it is just there when you meet someone special and you cannot explain it
My grandmother used to leave a lamp on the verandah at the edge of the forest every night until my grandfather came back from the fields.
doha with a lamp and a forest hut, about unstudied devotion
A lamp in the forest hut, a woman's patient hours; no scripture has written such a lesson as she lives.
lamp in the forest
Beside the edge of a forest, a lamp glows in a hut where a woman waits, and she learned to wait without any teaching. Compose a doha on devotion not learned in books but lived through a quiet night.
sword, river, tenderness

A soldier lays down his sword by the river each evening and sits quietly with his wife, and neither has ever read a word about how to cherish one another. Write a doha on tenderness learned only by living together.
My brother put down his sword of an argument by the river, hugged his rival, and said nothing; no book could have made him do that.
doha on affection nobody teaches, a sword and a river in it pls
Sword laid aside at the river's edge, two hearts sit unschooled, and the water carries their lesson on.
jaggery and the churn

My grandmother gave me a piece of jaggery whenever I was sad and churned her own butter for me every morning, never explaining a thing. Compose a doha: affection is tasted and lived, never read from any book.
My mother never said she adored me, she just kept a lump of jaggery in the cupboard and churned buttermilk for me after every exam.
Jaggery teaches sweetness on the palate and the churn teaches patience in the arm; the heart has no other books.
hey doha: caring is tasted not read, jaggery plus a churn
She weighs salt and grain on the old scales at her shop all day, but when her husband limps in she measures nothing and serves him first. Write a doha about devotion no balance can weigh.
salt and scales, tenderness
Salt and scales belong to the shopkeeper; the heart's tenderness is weighed by none and learned by none.
can u do a doha, affection cant be weighed, salt and scales
My mother used to say you cannot weigh affection on scales or season it with salt, and she cooked for us as if that were proof.
traveler learns tenderness
doha pls: a traveler is taught real affection by a stranger's kindness
The traveler asks the road how to cherish, and the road replies that every step is the lesson.
A traveler stopped in a village, and a stranger shared her last meal with him, never having read a word on hospitality or devotion, simply one heart to another. Please write a doha on that.
My father was a traveler for months at a time, and each time he returned my mother just stood silent at the gate; I saw they knew something I hadn't learned.
untaught tenderness
Untaught, the heart bows before its beloved, and no scholar can say how.
I asked my mother when she learned to cherish my father, and she laughed and said she never learned, it just stayed.
doha on the thing no one has ever managed to teach: affection

Scholars have gathered round the question of how to adore another, and the answer was in a mother's hands, a bride's shyness and a father's silence on the doorstep, not in any page that was ever written down.
the unwritten look
The best book on affection I ever saw was the face of an old man looking at his wife across a crowded room, and no author could have written it. Please compose a long doha on this idea.
doha: nobody writes it right, real caring is just seen
Let the learned write their volumes; one look across a crowded room has already said everything.
Honestly the thing that taught me real care was watching my parents quietly argue and then share the last piece of cake.
